Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, Git-Bash/PowerShell environment). Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies allowed.

CONTEXT — read fully before writing anything:
- lib/site-records.ts, lib/site-endpoint.ts, lib/site-forms.ts — the Phase 0 foundation just built. `SiteRecord` (prisma/schema.prisma) has `id, projectId, kind (generic string), fields (generic Json), status (default "active"), ipHash, spam, createdAt, updatedAt`. Writes happen via same-origin-only `POST /__records/<kind>` (form-action 'self', no CSP relaxation, no client JS/fetch) — the generated page never does anything but a plain HTML form POST/navigation.
- app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts — GET handler for published sites. Note `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`: every page is served fresh per request from `db.projectFile`, not a frozen snapshot. This is what makes B below possible without any client-side JS or CSP change.
- lib/agent.ts — the system prompt the builder model receives. Find where it currently explains `src/pages/`, the form pattern (`/__forms/<name>`, `_gotcha`/`_t`/`_next` control fields), and the general "what generated sites can and cannot do" framing (features.ts's NOT_OFFERED list is relevant background — this work does NOT change any of those hard blockers like live chat, checkout, etc.; SiteRecord is a genuinely new, separate real capability, additive to that list, not a workaround for it).
- app/projects/[id]/records/ — the owner's authenticated dashboard view of SiteRecords, just built. Read it fully.
- lib/site-forms.ts's escaping discipline (`escapeHtml`, "never HTML-escapes at storage, only at each output boundary") — this is the exact rule you must follow anywhere you inject SiteRecord field values into HTML.

THE GOAL (confirmed scope — do NOT include real user accounts/login, that is explicitly deferred to later separate work):

**A — Teach the builder to design its own record shapes.** Extend lib/agent.ts's system prompt with a new section (parallel in tone/rigor to the existing forms section) explaining SiteRecord to the model: it can `POST /__records/<kind>` to store structured data for whatever the business actually needs — a CRM's contacts, a restaurant's reservations, a shop's inventory, a gym's class roster, anything — by choosing its own `kind` (URL-safe token, same regex discipline as form names) and its own field names (same regex/cap discipline as form fields: validated key names, capped value lengths, `_`-prefixed control fields never stored). It is NOT a fixed template — the model picks the shape that fits the brief. Explain the full lifecycle it now has available (write via A, read-back via B, update/cancel via C) so it can build something that is actually a working data-backed feature, not just a write-only form. Be exact about the mechanics (exact path shape, exact control-field names, exact content-type) since this text steers a model that will generate real markup — copy the existing forms section's level of precision.

**B — Real reads: live data rendered back into the page, server-side, per request, with zero client JS and zero CSP change.** Design and implement a minimal, SAFE server-side templating convention:
- The builder authors a container element with `data-kodely-records="<kind>"` and, inside it, exactly one `<template data-kodely-record-template>` child whose innerHTML is the per-record markup, using `{{fieldName}}` placeholders ONLY in text content (never inside tag attributes like `src=`/`href=`/`on*=` — do not implement attribute interpolation at all, text-content-only, to close off any injection vector through attributes). The container's own children OTHER than the `<template>` (e.g., a paragraph inside it) serve as the empty-state fallback the builder authors itself.
- At GET-request time (in the same route that already reads db.projectFile and serves HTML — app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts), after loading an `.html` file's content and BEFORE the existing applySeo() step, scan for every `data-kodely-records="<kind>"` container, query `SiteRecord` where `projectId` matches and `kind` matches and `status: "active"` and `spam: false`, ordered newest-first, capped at a sane max (e.g. 100) so a page can never render unboundedly large. For EACH matching record, clone the `<template>`'s inner markup and replace every `{{fieldName}}` occurrence in TEXT NODES with that record's `fields[fieldName]` value, HTML-escaped exactly the way lib/site-forms.ts already escapes stored field values before they reach any HTML/email context (reuse or mirror escapeHtml exactly — never trust a field value in HTML unescaped). A field name with no matching value in that record renders as empty string, not as the literal `{{...}}` or an error — a record simply may not have every field the template expects. If there are zero matching records, leave the container's original static children in place (the builder's own empty-state) instead of an empty div. Remove the `<template>` tag itself from the served output in both cases (it's a build-time-authored template, not something a browser should ever be asked to render). This must run efficiently for a page with several containers (batch the SiteRecord queries per kind rather than one query per container if a page happens to have more than one of the same kind — should not normally happen, but don't do an unbounded number of separate queries per request either).
- No client-side JavaScript, no fetch, no CSP relaxation anywhere. This is pure server-side string/DOM templating done once per request in the existing route handler.
- Write a focused unit-style sanity check is not required (no test framework mandate here) but DO manually reason through: a record whose field VALUE contains `</template>`, `<script>`, or `{{` must render as inert escaped text, never break out of its slot or execute. State in your final report how you verified this (e.g., a specific field value you traced through the code by hand).

**C — Real update/cancel without accounts, via an unguessable per-record link (the same pattern real-world "manage your booking" email links use).**
- When a `SiteRecord` is created via `POST /__records/<kind>`, generate a cryptographically random token (Node's `crypto.randomBytes`, no new dependency), store only its SHA-256 hash on the row (add an `editTokenHash` nullable String column to the `SiteRecord` model — mirror how `ipHash` is already salted-hashed in this codebase, same salt-env-var pattern), and return the RAW token to the submitter exactly once, in the same-origin HTML response page (the existing `page()`-style reply in site-records.ts) as a real, copyable "manage this" link: `/__records/<kind>/<id>?token=<rawToken>`. If the submitted fields include a plausible email address (reuse the existing `replyToFor`-style strict email regex from lib/site-forms.ts, do not invent a looser one), ALSO state in that reply that the same link can be reached again by anyone with the record's id+token, so losing it isn't necessarily fatal, but do NOT implement actual emailing of this link in this pass — that's an enhancement for later, keep this pass's scope to generating and returning the token.
- New endpoint(s), same-origin only (extend the existing dispatch in app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts's POST handler): `POST /__records/<kind>/<id>` with a `_token` control field and either `_action=update` (replace the stored `fields` with the newly submitted ones, same validation discipline as create) or `_action=cancel` (set `status` to `"cancelled"`, do NOT hard-delete — matches the existing schema comment that status exists precisely so history isn't destroyed). Reject with an honest, generic "that link isn't valid" reply (do not distinguish "wrong token" from "record not found" in the response — same anti-enumeration discipline lib/site-forms.ts already uses for its 404s) if the id doesn't exist, the token hash doesn't match, or the kind doesn't match the record's actual kind.
- The project OWNER (authenticated, in app/projects/[id]/records/) does not need a token — they already have real ownership via the existing auth+project-ownership check that page uses. Add real update/cancel controls there too (the owner can cancel/edit any record on their own project without a token, since they're already authenticated as its owner) — read that page's existing patterns (Card/Badge/Button usage) and match them.
- All of this stays inside the exact same safety machinery as Phase 0: same host/origin checks, same body caps, same rate limiting (reuse lib/site-endpoint.ts's shared helpers, don't duplicate).

CONSTRAINTS (non-negotiable):
- Do not build any accounts/login/session system — explicitly deferred.
- Do not add `connect-src` or any other CSP relaxation to SANDBOX_CSP in app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts. Everything in B and C must work via server-side rendering and same-origin form POSTs only.
- Do not implement attribute-position `{{}}` interpolation (text-content only, per B above) — this is a deliberate security boundary, not an oversight to "complete later."
- Do not hard-delete SiteRecord rows from the visitor-facing cancel path — only the status change.
- Keep `kind` and `fields` fully generic everywhere you touch them — no hardcoded "booking"/"reservation"/"listing" special-casing in validation or rendering logic (illustrative examples in lib/agent.ts's prompt text are fine and expected, since the model needs concrete examples to learn the pattern from — the constraint is on the CODE's logic, not on illustrative prose).
- Schema change: add `editTokenHash` to `SiteRecord` (nullable). Do NOT run `prisma migrate dev`, `prisma db push`, or any DB-touching command yourself — write the schema change and tell me in your final report that `npx prisma db push` (this project's established convention, confirmed working) needs to be run, so I can do it.

STEPS:
1. Read every file listed above in full before writing code.
2. Implement A (lib/agent.ts prompt section).
3. Implement B (the template-rendering step in the site route's GET handler, with the escaping discipline stated above).
4. Implement C (token generation on create, the new update/cancel endpoint, the owner-side UI controls).
5. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish. If `tsc` complains about the new `editTokenHash` field not existing on the Prisma client type, that's expected until the schema is pushed and the client regenerated — note it in your report rather than trying to run the DB command yourself.

Report back: exactly how the `{{fieldName}}` escaping is enforced (walk through the injection-attempt trace you reasoned through), the exact new endpoint shapes, where the owner-side edit/cancel controls live, and the exact command I need to run.

The CSP sets no font-src, so fonts fall back to default-src 'self', which does NOT allow data: (unlike img-src, which does). A base64 font is blocked exactly like a remote one. 71 72 ## Quality bar 73 Ship something that looks designed, not templated. Real, specific copy for the 74 subject at hand — never "Lorem ipsum" and never placeholder headings like 75 "Your Title Here". Responsive down to 380px. Semantic HTML, labelled form 76 controls, sufficient colour contrast, and a visible :focus style. Include a 77 dark-mode treatment unless the brief implies otherwise. 21	 *
22	 * Two shapes, because the proxy rewrites the branded subdomain onto an
23	 * internal path:
24	 *   <slug>.kodely.site/         -> internally /api/site/<slug>
25	 *   staging.kodely.me/api/site/<slug>/   (no wildcard DNS off prod)

27	 * Canonical/OG URLs must use the EXTERNAL form or they point somewhere the
28	 * visitor's browser never went, so this keys off the Host header.
29	 */
30	export function siteBaseUrl(req: Request, slug: string): string {
31	  const host = req.headers.get("host") ?? "";
32	  const bare = host.split(":")[0];
33	
34	  // Deliberately NOT derived from x-forwarded-proto. Cloudflare's SSL mode
35	  // here is Flexible: it terminates TLS at the edge and talks to the origin
36	  // over plain HTTP, so nginx forwards `x-forwarded-proto: http` even though
37	  // the visitor is on https. Trusting it emitted http:// canonical and og:url
38	  // on sites that are only reachable over https.
39	  //
40	  // That was invisible in testing because Cloudflare's Automatic HTTPS
41	  // Rewrites silently repairs href="http://..." (canonical) but NOT
42	  // content="http://..." (og:url) — so only the OG tag stayed wrong, and
43	  // only when checked through the real edge.
44	  //
45	  // Every published site is reachable only via the Cloudflare HTTPS edge, so
46	  // anything that isn't loopback is https by definition.
47	  const isLocal = bare === "localhost" || bare === "127.0.0.1" || bare === "::1";
48	  const proto = isLocal ? "http" : "https";
49	  // Branded subdomain: the site lives at the host root.
50	  if (bare.endsWith(`.${SITES_BASE}`)) return `${proto}://${host}`;
51	  // Otherwise it is served under a path (staging, localhost).
52	  return `${proto}://${host}/api/site/${slug}`;
53	}

60	 * document per page, and the site route serves `about.html` for a request to

277	 * also what makes the dedupe real rather than cosmetic: about.html and
278	 * /about.html were already collapsed, but so are about.html and about/index.html
279	 * — two files that would otherwise have listed the same page twice.
280	 */
281	export function sitemapXml(baseUrl: string, htmlPaths: string[], lastMod?: Date): string {
282	  const seen = new Set<string>();
283	  const urls = htmlPaths
284	    .map((p) => pageUrl(baseUrl, p))
285	    .filter((u) => (seen.has(u) ? false : (seen.add(u), true)))
286	    .map((u) => {
287	      const loc = escapeXml(u);
288	      const mod = lastMod ? `\n    <lastmod>${lastMod.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}</lastmod>` : "";
289	      return `  <url>\n    <loc>${loc}</loc>${mod}\n  </url>`;
290	    })
291	    .join("\n");
292	  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">\n${urls}\n</urlset>\n`;

**Escaping trace (how I verified the injection cases by hand):** `renderTemplate()` splits the *static, builder-authored* template inner-HTML via `templateInner.split(/(<[^>]*>)/)` **before** any record data is touched — this produces alternating text/tag segments. The `{{field}}` substitution regex only runs over the non-tag (even-indexed) segments; tag segments are copied through completely untouched, which is what makes attribute-position interpolation structurally impossible rather than just discouraged in prose. For a record whose field value is `</template>`: since the template boundaries were already fixed from the *original* static markup before substitution, inserting `</template>` (via `escapeHtml`, which the module imports from `lib/site-endpoint.ts` — same function used everywhere else) into a text segment cannot re-open or re-close any tag; it's inert escaped text in the final output, and the real `<template>` tag has already been stripped from what's served either way. Same for `<script>` → `<script>` (inert text, never re-parsed as a tag). For `{{` in a value: `String.replace` with a global regex is a single non-recursive pass over the *original* string, so a value containing literal `{{name}}` is inserted as escaped output text (braces aren't HTML metacharacters) with no re-interpretation or infinite loop.
